config.title: Build pagination filter sort API pattern

intro.title: Build pagination filter sort API pattern
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a REST API endpoint that supports pagination, filtering, and sorting for a list of data. You'll learn how to handle query parameters to control the number of results, filter by specific fields, and sort the output. The core concept involves processing HTTP request queries and applying them to manipulate an in-memory dataset. You'll use Node.js with its built-in modules to create a server and manage the API logic. By the end, you'll have a functional API that can efficiently return tailored data based on user input.
intro.usecase: Pagination, filtering, and sorting are fundamental patterns in data-driven applications where users need to navigate large datasets efficiently. You'll find this pattern in e-commerce product listings where customers filter by category, sort by price, and browse through pages of results. It's equally essential in admin dashboards displaying user records, analytics platforms showing metrics, or content management systems organizing articles. As a backend developer, implementing robust pagination-filter-sort APIs ensures your applications remain performant and scalable while providing intuitive data exploration experiences.

objectives: Construct an Express route handler that accepts query parameters for pagination, filtering, and sorting.
Apply query parameter parsing logic to extract and validate page, limit, and sort criteria.
Implement a filtering mechanism that dynamically builds database queries based on user-provided criteria.
Configure a sorting system that orders query results by specified fields and directions.
Manipulate a dataset to return a paginated subset using calculated skip and limit values.
Integrate pagination metadata (total pages, current page) into the API response structure.
Initialize a test suite to verify the combined functionality of pagination, filtering, and sorting endpoints.

steps.title: Define pagination helper function
steps.instruction: Create a function named paginate that takes three parameters: data (array), page (number), and limit (number). Inside the function, calculate the start index and return the appropriate slice of the data array.
steps.hint: The start index can be calculated as (page - 1) * limit. Use the slice() method to return the portion of the array from start index to start index + limit.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a reusable paginate function that can slice any array based on page number and items per page.
successCriteria: The paginate function is defined with three parameters and returns the correct slice of data based on page and limit values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it takes all three parameters and returns the sliced array using the correct calculation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paginate function isn't working yet. Remember it needs to calculate start index as (page - 1) * limit and return data.slice(start, start + limit).

steps.title: Define filtering helper function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'filterData' that takes two parameters: 'data' (an array of items) and 'filters' (an object). Inside the function, use the array's filter method to return items where the category matches filters.category (if provided) and the name includes filters.search (if provided).
steps.hint: Start with 'function filterData(data, filters) { ... }' or 'const filterData = (data, filters) => { ... }'. Use data.filter(item => { ... }). Check if filters.category exists and matches item.category, and if filters.search exists and item.name includes it (case-insensitive).
steps.expectedOutcome: A filterData function is defined that can filter an array based on category and search criteria from a filters object.
successCriteria: The filterData function is defined with two parameters (data, filters), uses the filter method, and returns filtered data based on category and search criteria.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the filterData function, but check that it handles both category and search filters properly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The filterData function is missing or doesn't filter correctly. Ensure it takes two parameters and uses the filter method with proper conditions.

steps.expectedOutcome: A sortData function is defined that can sort an array by a given field in ascending or descending order.
successCriteria: The sortData function is defined with three parameters (data, field, order) and returns a sorted array.
